{{Current events|year=2018|month=05|day=8|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**A [[war crimes]] tribunal in [[Colombia]] begins investigating atrocities during the war which began in the 1960s. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/05/war-crimes-tribunal-investigating-colombias-war-atrocities-180508165257023.html (al-Jazeera)]
*[[Bosnia]]n prosecutors appeal the acquittal of [[Naser Oric]], former commander of the [[Bosnian Army]] in [[Srebrenica]], who was accused of killing Serb prisoners. [http://www.balkaninsight.com/en/article/bosnian-prosecution-appeals-naser-oric-war-crimes-acquittal-05-08-2018 (Balkan Insight)]

;Business and economy
*The heads of [[Serco]] and [[Mitie]] are expected to appear before the [[UK]]'s [[Public Administration and Constitutional Affairs Select Committee]] to testify over the collapse of [[Carillion]]. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2018/05/07/serco-mitie-bosses-face-mps-carillion-collapse/ (''The Telegraph'')]
*[[President of Argentina]] [[Mauricio Macri]] announces talks with the [[International Monetary Fund]] on financial support for the country's economy. The [[Central Bank of Argentina]] interest rate is now at 40%, inflation at 25% and the value of the [[Argentine peso]] at a record low. [http://www.bbc.com/news/business-44047113 (BBC)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Grenfell Tower fire]]
**''[[The Guardian]]'' reports that the [[Grenfell Tower]] in [[London]], which burned down last year with the loss of 72 lives, received a quote for non-flammable cladding but it was rejected for a more expensive option which exacerbated the fire. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2018/may/08/grenfell-tower-more-costly-fire-resistant-cladding-plan-was-dropped (''The Guardian'')]

;International relations
*[[China–North Korea relations]]
**For the second time in [[Kim–Xi meeting|two months]], [[North Korea]] leader [[Kim Jong-un]] meets [[China]] president [[Xi Jinping]], this time in [[Dalian]]. [https://i.stuff.co.nz/world/asia/103743798/north-korean-leader-kim-jong-un-meets-chinese-president-again-before-trump-summit (Stuff)]
*[[United States withdrawal from the Iran Deal]]
**[[Donald Trump]] announces that the [[United States]] [[United States withdrawal from the Iran Deal|withdraws]] from the [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action|Iran Nuclear Deal]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2018/05/08/world/middleeast/trump-iran-nuclear-deal.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[Iran]] says that it remains committed to the agreement but also that it is ready to step up uranium enrichment. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/middle_east/iran-prepared-for-all-scenarios-if-trump-nixes-nuclear-deal-officials-say/2018/05/08/531047a0-5241-11e8-a6d4-ca1d035642ce_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

;Law and crime
*High profile [[China|Chinese]] [[Communist Party of China|Communist Party]] member [[Sun Zhengcai]] is sentenced to life in prison for taking bribes totaling 170 million yuan. [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-china-44036175 (BBC)]
*The [[Metropolitan Police]] of [[London]] announces a review of 21 [[rape]]s and [[sexual assault]]s as well as 12 other offences including violence and [[burglary|burglaries]] over inadequately performed "undeclared casework" by a forensic scientist. [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-44044668 (BBC)]
*[[Terrorism in Greece]]
**[[Greece|Greek]] officials arrest 14 men, all but one of which are [[Greek people|Greek nationals]], on suspicion of funding terrorism. [http://www.ekathimerini.com/228419/article/ekathimerini/news/14-arrested-on-terror-funding-charges (''Kathimerini'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2018 Armenian protests]], [[Politics of Armenia]] 
**[[Armenia]]'s [[Parliament of Armenia|parliament]] elects protest leader [[Nikol Pashinyan]] as the new [[Prime Minister of Armenia]]. [https://www.huffingtonpost.com/entry/armenia-prime-minister-election_us_5af17239e4b0c4f193267607 (The Huffington Post)]
*[[Brexit]]
**[[Theresa May]] confirms her trust in [[Boris Johnson]] after he called her post-Brexit trade policy with the [[European Union]] "crazy". [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-05-08/may-backs-johnson-after-he-attacks-her-crazy-brexit-trade-plan (Bloomberg)]
